content.overview: Biodiversity protection in India is supported by the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, which provides for conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of biological resources. Constitutional support appears in Articles 48A and 51A(g). The framework sits alongside wildlife protection, forest conservation, the EPA and NGT jurisdiction.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Access to biological resources or traditional knowledge? (2) Biodiversity Act approvals/institutions? (3) Benefit-sharing? (4) Link to wildlife/forest regimes?
content.study:
Distinguish biodiversity access and benefit-sharing from pure wildlife hunting/trade controls and forest-land conversion. Verify institutional names and approval routes against the current official text.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Biological Diversity Act 2002
sections.body: Conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use and equitable benefit-sharing from use of biological resources and associated knowledge.

sections.heading: Institutions
sections.body: National and State-level biodiversity authorities as constituted under the Act — approval and regulatory roles as enacted.

sections.heading: Access and benefit-sharing
sections.body: Access to biological resources and associated knowledge is regulated; benefit-sharing principles apply as the statute provides.

sections.heading: Constitutional support
sections.body: Art. 48A and Art. 51A(g) support environmental and wildlife protection including biodiversity values.

sections.heading: Coordination
sections.body: Wildlife (Protection) Act, Forest (Conservation) Act and EPA may apply concurrently on habitat and project facts.

examples.title: Access without approval
examples.body: Commercial use of a biological resource without the approval the Biodiversity Act requires — statutory access/benefit-sharing regime is attracted.

hypotheticals.question: Does wildlife sanctuary permission replace Biodiversity Act compliance?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not automatically. Wildlife area rules and biodiversity access/benefit-sharing are distinct statutory regimes.

distinctions.title: Biodiversity Act vs Wildlife (Protection) Act
distinctions.left: Access, sustainable use and benefit-sharing for biological resources.
distinctions.right: Protection of wild animals/birds/plants, hunting and protected areas.

misconceptions.trap: Biodiversity law is only about national parks.
misconceptions.correction: The Biological Diversity Act centres on conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit-sharing, not only protected-area management.
